priceSnapshot.note: The coil broke, and it broke DOWN. The morning report closed with lower highs into higher lows and said explicitly that a coil has no tilt and nobody knew which pole it would pick. It picked the floor. Price ran the 65,237.8 high at 12:00Z, failed the 65,300 add trigger by 62.2 points for the sixth consecutive time, and then lost 1,405.5 points in four hours to a 63,832.3 low. Two settled hourly closes now sit beneath the 64,650 reduce line - 64,298.0 at 15:00Z and 63,905.8 at 16:00Z - so the line that had been advertised UNCHANGED for thirteen sessions has FIRED for the first time. This was not a drift lower. Since the morning snapshot the market force-closed $10,377,727 of LONGS against $6,906 of shorts, a ratio of 1,503 to 1, and open interest fell 0.69% to $2,052,335,618. That is a genuine long flush, and it arrived on a macro trigger rather than a crypto one.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $63,750. This is a NEW line and it replaces the 64,650 level that fired this session. It is placed 18.7 points beneath the 4H EMA200 at 63,771.74, which is the single most important number on the board right now: it is the last moving average of any timeframe that price still holds, it sits 217.0 points, 0.34%, beneath spot, and the session low of 63,832.3 stopped 60.6 points above it without testing it. A settled hourly close beneath 63,750 means the 4H EMA200 failed on a close rather than a wick, which removes the last structural floor between here and the 63,000 handle and would confirm the daily EMA20 loss at 64,295.83 as a trend change rather than a shakeout.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE back above $64,650, WITH open interest holding or rising across the same bar. The price half is the retest-from-below of the exact line that just broke, and it is also the daily EMA50 neighbourhood at 64,683.13 and a $970,508 realized long-liquidation shelf - reclaiming it would mean the flush was a stop-run rather than a trend change. The open-interest half is retained verbatim from the previous four sessions because it has now scored on six consecutive tests, most recently this morning when it blocked a buy at 65,368.0 that would be 1,379 points underwater right now. A reclaim on FALLING open interest is short-covering and fades; a reclaim on rising open interest is real.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from ADD to REDUCE, and the reduce is being ACTED on rather than merely announced - the wallet sold 25% of the spot core at 63,988.7. This is the first REDUCE of the range and it is a rule firing, not a forecast: the 64,650 line was published unchanged for thirteen consecutive sessions with the confirmation 'a settled 1H close below', and two settled hourly closes have now printed beneath it. Honouring your own trigger when it fires against you is the entire point of writing it down in advance. Everything the morning listed as supportive has flipped inside six hours. Open interest went from FLAT at -0.018% to FALLING at -0.69%. The long/short account ratio, which was easing at 1.23, has risen to 1.45 as price fell - accounts got MORE long into a decline, which is how second legs get funded. 1H RSI collapsed from 47.31 to 24.96 and 15m RSI to 23.24. Price lost, in order and in four hours, the 1H EMA20, EMA50, EMA100 and finally the 1H EMA200 at 64,500.62, plus the daily EMA20 at 64,295.83 and the daily EMA50 at 64,683.13. The one thing that has NOT broken is the 4H EMA200 at 63,771.74, which is why the new reduce line sits just beneath it rather than at the current price.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is DOWN on three measured facts, not on sentiment. First, of the twelve largest clusters in the window, eleven are LONG-side and the single short-side cluster sits 1,311 points overhead. Second, open interest fell 0.69% to $2,052,335,618 across the decline, so positions were closed rather than opened - a deleveraging, and deleveragings usually need a second flush to finish. Third, and most important, the long/short account ratio ROSE from 1.23 at the morning snapshot to 1.45 now. Accounts got more long as price fell 1,192 points. That is the classic setup where the cluster at 63,850 gets revisited: the stops that fired have been replaced by fresh ones sitting in the same place.

etfFlows.note: No new print exists at the 12:42 COT snapshot. US spot bitcoin ETF flow data for Monday 10 August publishes after the 16:00 ET close, roughly 15:00 COT, so the standing figure is still Friday 07 August: a FIFTH consecutive session of net inflows at roughly $99-102 million depending on the aggregator, with IBIT +$86.7m and FBTC +$41m against a $19.4m BTCO outflow, capping a week above $750m. That streak is the strongest structural argument against reading today's flush as a trend change - the ETF bid does not trade hourly charts and did not sell this move, because it could not. It is also the single biggest thing to check at the endday session: if Monday prints the first OUTFLOW of the streak on a day BTC fell 1.9%, the higher-lows thesis that has held since 05 August loses its mechanism.

calibration.note: Two rules were tested this session and both did their job, in opposite directions. The 64,650 reduce line, published unchanged for thirteen consecutive sessions, FIRED on the 15:00Z close of 64,298.0 and was confirmed by the 16:00Z close of 63,905.8 - the first time it has triggered since it was written. The 65,300 add trigger did NOT fire for a sixth consecutive test: the session high of 65,237.8 stopped 62.2 points short, and had it fired the desk would have bought within 62 points of the day's high and be 1,249 points underwater four hours later. The morning's own action scored badly and is marked as such: it added 4 USDT of spot at 65,180.5, which is 1,191.8 points, 1.83%, above the current mark. The mitigating detail is size, not direction - the morning explicitly sized that add down from 11.98 available to 4 because the open-interest participation test had gone flat, so the rule that could not stop the loss did at least cap it at roughly 0.07 USDT of unrealized damage on that tranche.
